req.title: Login required for create
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /create.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-012 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users attempting GET /create are redirected to /auth/login with a 302 status. The violation in test[0] was kind=negative paired with heuristic=EP, which is logically inconsistent: EP (Equivalence Partitioning) is a positive-class heuristic used to identify representative valid inputs, not error/negative paths. Fix: change test[0] kind to 'positive' because the redirect IS the expected/correct system behaviour for an anonymous user — it is the happy-path outcome of the requirement. The test verifies the primary stated behaviour (302 to /auth/login), making it a positive test using EP. Tests [1] and [2] are preserved unchanged.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
    f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers.get("Location")}'
)

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

login_r = client.post(
    '/auth/login',
    data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'},
    follow_redirects=False
)
assert login_r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {login_r.status_code}'
r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'form' in r.data.lower(), 'Expected form element in create page'

tests.name: test_logout_then_get_create_redirects_again
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded data
actions: Send GET /create again with no session (anonymous state)
expected: Second GET /create Location header is exactly /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

client.post(
    '/auth/login',
    data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'},
    follow_redirects=False
)
r_auth = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
assert r_auth.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 while logged in, got {r_auth.status_code}'
logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout', follow_redirects=False)
assert logout_r.status_code == 302, f'Expected logout 302, got {logout_r.status_code}'
r_anon = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
assert r_anon.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 after logout, got {r_anon.status_code}'
assert r_anon.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
    f'Expected /auth/login, got {r_anon.headers.get("Location")}'
)
